patterns.usage_note: が links two clauses as a plain but, attaching to the plain form (高いが, 明日だが) or to the polite ます/です form (行きましたが), and it is more formal than けど, normal in writing and careful speech. Its siblings are the case particle が marking the subject (雨が降る) and the が marking the object of a stative predicate (日本語が分かる). It is often not adversative at all: 失礼ですが or 田中ですが simply prefaces what follows.

examples.ruby: 値段[ねだん]は高[たか]いが、この店[みせ]の味[あじ]は文句[もんく]なしだ。
examples.english: It's pricey, but you can't fault the food at this place.

examples.ruby: 切符[きっぷ]は買[か]ったが、電車[でんしゃ]の時間[じかん]を間違[まちが]えた。
examples.english: I bought the ticket, but I got the train time wrong.

examples.ruby: 今日[きょう]は寒[さむ]いが、妹[いもうと]は半袖[はんそで]で学校[がっこう]へ行[い]った。
examples.english: It's cold today, but my sister went off to school in short sleeves.

patterns.usage_note: Links two clashing clauses, the second going against what the first sets up (文句ばかり言うけど、頼めば手伝う). It is the conversational counterpart of が: けれども is the full form, けど the most casual and by far the commonest in speech. Like が it also works as a soft preface (すみませんけど) and can be left dangling to trail off (行きたいんですけど…).

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]は平気[へいき]で泳[およ]げるけども、私[わたし]は水[みず]が苦手[にがて]だ。
examples.english: My sister can swim without a second thought, but I'm no good in water.

examples.ruby: 傘[かさ]は持[も]ってきたけれども、結局[けっきょく]一度[いちど]も差[さ]さなかった。
examples.english: I brought an umbrella along, though in the end I never once put it up.

examples.ruby: 兄[あに]は文句[もんく]ばかり言[い]うけど、頼[たの]めば必[かなら]ず手伝[てつだ]う。
examples.english: My brother complains nonstop, but ask him and he'll always pitch in.

patterns.usage_note: Marks an unexpected reversal: the speaker did something and what followed contradicted what they had counted on (電話してみたところが、番号は変わっていた). Unlike が or けれども it requires that surprise, and the outcome clause typically reports a discovery rather than the speaker's own decision. The form is 〜たところが, with だ after voiced stems (呼んだところが); the が-less 〜たところ is now much more common, which leaves this one bookish.

examples.ruby: 電話[でんわ]してみたところが、番号[ばんごう]はすでに変[か]わっていた。
examples.english: I tried calling, only to find the number had already been changed.

examples.ruby: 大声[おおごえ]で呼[よ]んだところが、家[いえ]の中[なか]は静[しず]まり返[かえ]っていた。
examples.english: I called out at the top of my voice, and yet the house stayed dead silent.

examples.ruby: 弁当[べんとう]の蓋[ふた]を開[あ]けたところが、箸[はし]が入[はい]っていなかった。
examples.english: I opened the lid of my lunch box, only to find there were no chopsticks inside.

patterns.usage_note: Concessive ながら sets a persisting state against a clashing main clause: 新人ながら, 狭いながらも, 知っていながら, with one subject on both sides. A sibling entry takes the simultaneous reading, two actions at once (音楽を聞きながら歩く). After a ます-stem the two look alike; a stative verb such as 知っている gives the concessive reading, an action verb the simultaneous one.

examples.ruby: 狭[せま]いながらも、二人[ふたり]で暮[く]らすには十分[じゅうぶん]な部屋[へや]だ。
examples.english: It's cramped, but it's plenty of room for the two of us.

examples.ruby: 兄[あに]は事情[じじょう]を知[し]っていながら、何[なに]も教[おし]えてくれなかった。
examples.english: My brother knew perfectly well what was going on, and still told me nothing.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]は素人[しろうと]ながら、大会[たいかい]で堂々[どうどう]と踊[おど]りきった。
examples.english: Amateur though she was, my sister danced her whole routine at the meet with real poise.
